subject: general
question: What percentage of solar energy is captured by green plants in terrestrial ecosystem?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 percent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Green plants in terrestrial ecosystems capture only about **1 percent** of the solar energy that reaches them.
 
• This energy is utilized for the process of **photosynthesis**, where it is converted into chemical energy.
 
• The chemical energy is stored in the form of **glucose** and other organic molecules.
 
• The efficiency of solar energy capture by plants is relatively low due to various factors such as **reflection, transmission, and absorption of light** by non-photosynthetic parts.
 
• Despite the low percentage, this energy forms the base of the **food chain** in terrestrial ecosystems, supporting a wide range of life forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis**

 
 
• It is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy.
 
• Photosynthesis primarily occurs in the **chloroplasts** of plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transfer in Ecosystems**
 
 
• Energy captured by plants is transferred to herbivores when they consume plants, and subsequently to carnivores when they consume herbivores.
 
• Only about **10 percent** of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.
 
 
 
• **Solar Energy Utilization**
 
 
• A large portion of solar energy is not used for photosynthesis and is instead reflected or absorbed as heat.
 
• Plants have evolved various adaptations to maximize their **light absorption efficiency**.
